newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ANA half-year profits jump nearly 33 percent.
newsitem.headline: Japan ANA half-year profits jump nearly 33 percent.

text.p: All Nippon Airways (ANA) said on Thursday that its six-month profits jumped almost 33 percent as increased flights and passengers more than offset a rise in fuel prices.

Japan's second-largest airline company and largest domestic air carrier said its parent current profit rose 32.9 percent in the first half of the 1996/97 business year to 17.9 billion yen ($157 million), thanks to increased passenger numbers.
Japan's biggest air carrier Japan Airlines Co Ltd announced on Wednesday that the higher fuel costs and a slump in the yen had caused its half-year parent current profits to plunge 60.7 percent.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.

ANA also said its sales rose 5.1 percent from a year ago to 450.7 billion yen ($3.95 billion). A company spokesman said sales, although robust, were not as good as the company had expected at the beginning of the business year.
Higher fuel prices had some effect on the company's earnings, but it was able to offset that by increases in flights and passengers, the spokesman said.
The cost of fuel in the six-month period rose nine percent year-on-year, he said.
The number of passengers on ANA's domestic flights totalled 18.9 million, up 5.5 percent from a year ago. Of the total, passengers on international flights reached 1.21 million, up 17.4 percent.
ANA operates 100 domestic routes, as well as 42 international routes from Tokyo and Osaka.

Airlines pay more for imported fuel and aircraft replacement parts as result of the decline in the yen's value. A weak yen also makes overseas trips less attractive to Japanese, as it increases travelling expenses in terms of yen.
The yen stood at around 114 to the dollar on Thursday, compared with about 100 yen to the dollar a year ago.
ANA also revised down its full-year earnings forecast, due mainly to smaller-than-expected earnings in the first half.
The company now expects sales to total 880 billion yen ($7.71 billion), down three billion yen ($26.3 million) from the previous forecast.
Parent current profit was revised down from 18.5 billion yen ($162 million) to 17.5 billion yen ($153 million). ($1=114 yen)
